title: Important Ripple News and XRP Price Update: October 30
body: Ripple closed out a highly busy Swell 2026 conference with major announcements and developments involving some industry and TradFi giants such as Coinbase, Robinhood, and BNY, as well as major regulatory news. Meanwhile, XRP Ledger developers proposed tighter control for permissioned assets. However, Ripple’s cross-border token has slumped to new local lows. Ripple News Perhaps the most notable takeaway for the XRP Army from Swell came directly from CEO Brad Garlinghouse, who pushed back against concerns that the company’s rapidly expanding RLUSD business has sidelined XRP. He described the latter as the firm’s “North Star,” saying Ripple only wants to pursue activities that benefit the cross-border token. Nevertheless, he acknowledged that RLUSD or fiat currencies can be more appropriate for certain financial transactions. The stablecoin itself received several significant boosts that prompted the aforementioned claims within the Ripple community. Coinbase expanded access across several of its platforms, including Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange, and its retail app, with support spanning XRPL, Ethereum, and Base. Ripple also unveiled a broader partnership with Robinhood, under which RLUSD will play a role across Bitstamp, institutional settlement, and eventually the main application. Vlad Tenev’s company will integrate Ripple Treasury into its internal financial operations. Separately, BNY expanded custody support to XRP and RLUSD, while Moody’s assigned the stablecoin an A2 long-term and P-1 short-term investment-grade rating, with the latter representing the agency’s highest short-term grade under its stablecoin framework. Ripple said its product revenue run rate is approaching $900 million annually. The company also received final OCC approval to establish Ripple National Trust Bank, giving it a federally supervised entity designed to support RLUSD reserves and institutional digital-asset custody. Ripple’s corporate-finance ambitions also grew, with Ripple Treasury bringing together AI-powered cash management, payments, forecasting, and liquidity tools, including 24/7 Returns for eligible businesses holding qualifying digital assets such as RLUSD. XRPL Developments The XRP Ledger is also receiving new institutional use cases as Ripple and C2FO are working to bring the latter’s Instant Pay settlement platform onto XRPL. They also want to use RLUSD to help suppliers receive funds in seconds rather than waiting days for conventional bank transfers to clear. XRPL devs proposed four code changes designed to tighten restrictions around permissioned tokens, such as regulated stablecoins or tokenized funds that issuers only want approved accounts to hold. The proposed fixCleanup3_5_0 upgrade would close several remaining exceptions, including routes involving automated market makers, and would generally restrict unapproved holders to returning tokens to their issuer until authorization is granted. At the same time, Flare joined the XRPL validator list, while the XRP Ledger Foundation dropped Anodos Finance since the project requested to be removed ahead of a planned validator shutdown by the end of the month. XRP Price Update Although Ripple had quite the impressive second part of October, the underlying token has fallen with the rest of the market. XRP was rejected at $1.40 on October 21 and the subsequent correction pushed it south to $1.25. It rebounded in the following days and challenged $1.35 after the Fed paused interest rate hikes on Wednesday. However, the largest hack against any crypto exchange that unfolded earlier this morning resulted in a market-wide crash that drove XRP to a multi-month low of $1.19. Despite recovering slightly since then, the asset remains 4% down on the day. It has slipped by 6% weekly, while its market cap has tanked to under $80 billion. title: Bitcoin or Dollars: What Stays Fixed in a Betting Budget?
body: Setting aside Bitcoin (BTC) for sports betting leaves a basic question unresolved: is the budget fixed in digital coins or in US dollars? Keeping the same BTC quantity does not preserve the same dollar value when the exchange rate changes. A dollar budget works differently: its stated value stays fixed, while the corresponding Bitcoin quantity varies. The distinction begins before any funds leave a wallet. BitPay’s July 2026 portfolio tracking update describes a total portfolio valuation alongside breakdowns by wallet and token. Those views answer different questions. A coin balance records quantity; its dollar valuation expresses that quantity at a particular price. With an unchanged BTC balance, price movement alone can alter the dollar figure. Neither display, by itself, identifies how much someone has decided to allocate to betting. Decide what the budget measures Bitcoin can be the asset used for funding while dollars remain the currency used to measure the budget. That measuring currency is the unit of account. Specifying it gives “the same amount” a precise meaning. For a budget defined in BTC , the limit is the chosen coin quantity. For one defined in dollars, it is the chosen dollar amount. Those figures can be equivalent at one exchange rate and diverge later. Recording both is useful, provided that the budget states which measure controls the allocation. For sports betting at Lucky Rebel , a personal allowance can be defined in dollars, even when Bitcoin is the funding method. The budget’s currency and the asset sent are separate choices. A wallet’s total balance may include funds for other purposes, so it should not automatically be treated as the betting pool. A stake is the amount committed to an individual sports bet . Defining the overall betting allowance comes first. A changed dollar valuation of coins awaiting transfer does not, on its own, represent a decision to change that allowance or the size of individual stakes. Record the valuation time The calculation is straightforward: multiply the Bitcoin quantity by the exchange rate expressed in dollars per Bitcoin. The result is a dollar valuation at that rate. Working backward, dividing a dollar amount by the same rate gives the corresponding BTC quantity. A valuation needs a timestamp as well as a price. Comparing a wallet’s current dollar value with an earlier figure combines two observations made at different times. Unless the coin quantities match, the difference could reflect both a price movement and a change in the amount held. A useful record therefore keeps the BTC quantity, reference currency, exchange rate, and valuation time together. Keep the original budget amount and its stated currency in separate fields. Updating the current value then preserves the distinction between what was allocated and what the earmarked coins are worth at the recorded rate. The resulting value is a planning figure. It does not promise the exchange rate available for a conversion or establish what a sportsbook will credit. Any fees and any difference between the reference rate and the actual conversion rate belong in the transaction record alongside the amount transferred. Give the allocation a defined period An amount also needs a time boundary. A budget for a season and an allowance for a single weekend describe different commitments, even when both use dollars. Writing down the period helps distinguish one continuing allocation from a fresh decision to assign funds. A fixed deposit amount also differs from a fixed budget for the period. Reusing the same BTC quantity for separate deposits describes a consistent transfer size. It does not establish the total assigned to an entire season. The record needs to distinguish the amount of each transfer from the overall allowance, so that “unchanged” refers to the intended limit, rather than just a recurring payment amount. This bankroll-management guide defines the betting pool separately from essentials and discusses setting it for a season, a year, or another period. Applied to crypto funding, that approach needs one further detail: the currency in which the pool is defined. Its duration says when the allocation applies; its denomination says what amount is being held constant. Record the start and end of that period alongside the stated amount. A later transfer can then be assigned to the relevant period rather than treated as an automatic renewal. When funds are earmarked before they are sent, the allocation date and transfer date need not match. What a dollar peg changes A stablecoin changes the valuation question, but the reference currency still needs to be explicit. Ledger’s explanation of stablecoins describes tokens designed to track another asset, commonly the US dollar. A dollar-linked token therefore targets a dollar value rather than following Bitcoin’s market price. That design is not a guarantee that its market price will always equal its target. The peg also does not fix value in every currency. A budget measured in British pounds still depends on the dollar-to-pound exchange rate when its funds are held in a dollar-linked token. Even if the token maintains its dollar target, its pound valuation can change. Before comparing two budget figures, check whether they describe the same coin quantity or the same reference currency amount over the same period. Keep the valuation timestamp alongside them. That record separates an actual change to the betting allowance from a different price applied to coins already set aside.

title: Standard Chartered Warns: “Bitcoin and Altcoin Decline May Continue After Binance Crisis, This Altcoin Could Be the Winner!”
body: The cryptocurrency market faced intense selling pressure following the approximately $6.3 billion security breach targeting Binance. Major cryptocurrencies, particularly Bitcoin and Ethereum, lost value. Sharp Drop in Bitcoin and Ethereum! Following the hack news, sell-offs accelerated in the cryptocurrency market. Bitcoin fell by over 3%, dropping to around $76,000, while Ethereum also fell below $2,200. According to the data, approximately $1.5 billion worth of leveraged positions were liquidated in the market within 24 hours, with the majority of these liquidations consisting of long positions opened with the expectation of an upward trend. Standard Chartered: The Decline May Continue! While the decline has unnerved the market, banking giant Standard Chartered warned that the market downturn may not be over yet. Speaking to Coindesk, Geoffrey Kendrick, Head of Digital Assets Research at Standard Chartered, stated that selling pressure following the Binance attack could continue for some time. According to Kendrick, for a new balance to be established in the market, the status of the frozen assets must be clarified and the details of the attack must be revealed. Kendrick also noted that the attack could accelerate investors’ shift towards decentralized trading platforms, a development that could support Uniswap’s long-term growth potential. He added that the bank maintains its UNI price target of $100 for 2030. Kendrick also stated that the Binance attack was a new development that strengthened the possibility of exceeding their previously predicted price forecast. *This is not investment advice. title: Moodys Opens The XRP Floodgates
body: A major credit rating from Moody’s has given RLUSD a new level of recognition from traditional finance, and Digital Asset Investor believes the development could have broader implications for XRP. In a video attached to his X post , he described the announcement as potentially the biggest among several recent developments involving RLUSD, BNY, and Coinbase. His comments came after Ripple SVP of Stablecoins Jack McDonald announced that Moody’s Ratings had assigned RLUSD an A2 long-term rating and a P-1 short-term rating. The P-1 rating represents Moody’s highest short-term rating category under its stablecoin framework. Moodys Opens The XRP Floodgates pic.twitter.com/HXgZzvQYoA — Digital Asset Investor (@digitalassetbuy) October 28, 2026 Moody’s Gives RLUSD Institutional Recognition Digital Asset Investor focused heavily on the distinction between RLUSD and competing stablecoins. He noted that USDT and USDC do not currently hold the same Moody’s ratings under this framework, while RLUSD has received both an A2 long-term rating and P-1 short-term rating. The ratings apply to RLUSD issued through Standard Custody & Trust Company, Ripple’s New York-regulated subsidiary. Moody’s assessment also takes into account RLUSD’s reserve structure, which maintains more than 103% reserve coverage, primarily through short-term U.S. Treasury bills and cash. For institutions, a formal credit assessment can provide an additional reference point when evaluating settlement assets, liquidity instruments, and counterparty risks. That distinction becomes important as stablecoins increasingly move beyond crypto-native markets and into institutional financial operations. BNY and Coinbase Add to the Institutional Push Digital Asset Investor also connected the Moody’s announcement with developments involving BNY and Coinbase. BNY serves as the primary custodian for RLUSD’s reserve assets, giving the stablecoin infrastructure a connection to one of the largest financial institutions in the United States. Coinbase has also expanded support for RLUSD across its retail and institutional platforms. Together, these developments give RLUSD access to established financial infrastructure while Ripple continues to expand its presence across payments , custody, banking, and digital asset services. Digital Asset Investor referred to these developments collectively before making his broader XRP claim. “Folks, you don’t have to be a math genius to figure out where XRP is going,” he said. “XRP is at the center of all of it.” Why XRP Matters to the RLUSD Expansion RLUSD and XRP serve different functions, but their activity can intersect through the XRP Ledger. RLUSD transactions on XRPL require XRP for network fees, while increased stablecoin activity can contribute to greater usage of the ledger. Higher RLUSD adoption could also support deeper liquidity across XRPL markets, potentially creating additional opportunities for XRP to function within cross-border liquidity flows. However, RLUSD growth does not automatically translate into proportional demand for XRP. A stablecoin can increase its supply and transaction volume without creating a one-to-one increase in XRP purchases. Still, Digital Asset Investor sees the combination of Moody’s rating, BNY custody, Coinbase support, and Ripple’s expanding financial infrastructure as evidence of a broader institutional push. For him, XRP’s role within that ecosystem makes the latest RLUSD development particularly significant. Disclaimer : This content is meant to inform and should not be considered financial advice. title: Here’s how Elon Musk reacted to the Binance hack
body: Elon Musk’s initial reaction to the massive $6.3 billion Binance hack that took place on Thursday, October 29, was a stark warning about the need for constant vigilance when it comes to cybersecurity. Specifically, the CEO of Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA ) and SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX ) published an X post simply stating that ‘Everyday is Zeroday.’ Everyday is Zeroday https://t.co/6eIeFNc4jZ — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 29, 2026 In cybersecurity, a zero-day refers to a previously unknown firmware, hardware, or software vulnerability that can be used by attackers. It is known as such since developers have zero days to address the issue before it gets exploited. Musk’s remark appears to have been justified since the hackers were allegedly able to inject malicious code that was tested earlier on the same day as the attack itself, enabling them to take control of Binance’s hot wallets, per a TRM analysis conveyed by Finbold on October 30. Elon Musk ‘trolls’ CZ over the Binance hack Elsewhere, not all of Elon Musk’s remarks have been as restrained as his initial reaction. For example, he took to laughing at a different X user comparing Binance’s claims that user funds are safe to similar reassurances issued by Sam Bankman-Fried during the collapse of FTX. The founder of the robbed cryptocurrency exchange, Changpeng Zhao (CZ), seemingly didn’t take kindly to the ‘trolling’ alluding to the possibility that the firm’s stake in SpaceX might be used to help cover the losses. CZ, however, later walked back on the proposal, claiming he intended the remark to show Binance has sufficient funds to weather the storm rather than hint at a SPCX stock sale. Why Elon Musk’s warning must be taken seriously Lastly, the previous 2026 trends in digital asset hacking and the October 29 incident indicate that Elon Musk’s warning should be taken very seriously. Cryptocurrency theft accelerated in the third quarter (Q3) to $1.17 billion – up nearly $200 billion from the Q1 and Q2 total – and the Binance attack alone is 180% bigger than the total for the first nine months of 2026. Furthermore, digital asset firms are not the only institutions to be targeted in recent months. The Revolut neobank was a victim of a phishing attack that affected the data of some of its more affluent clients in September. Simultaneously, the rise of artificial intelligence ( AI ) technology and the existing and expected breakthroughs in quantum computing could further exacerbate the issues, with some estimates predicting that Bitcoin ( BTC ) could reach its ‘doomsday’ as soon as March 2028 . title: CZ tells Musk 'bad time to troll' amid $6.3 billion Binance hack
body: Elon Musk’s keyboard warrior persona has drawn a public response from Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ), who called out unhelpful comments from the Tesla founder and X owner as crypto’s largest exchange deals with the industry’s largest security breach. CZ’s response came within hours of Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, with the exchange’s former CEO reminding Musk of an earlier $500 million Binance cash injection into the 2022 deal to buy Twitter. Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop. Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion. Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks! — CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 30, 2026 That stake has since doubled and is now worth over $1 billion. CZ responds to Musk’s public trolling CZ asked Elon to “Please stop” and “show a little support” earlier today, after multiple posts from the billionaire appeared to be poking fun at Binance’s situation as the exchange deals with the fallout of its $6.3 billion hack. Even in his response, CZ noted that he holds Musk in high regard, writing : “Elon, I have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll.” CZ reminded Musk of past business dealings with Binance, when the exchange committed about $500 million to Musk’s 2022 bid to acquire Twitter for $44 billion. The request was in response to a loaded post from Musk , who shared a grimacing emoji to a thread about the Binance hack. CZ responded to another attempt by Musk to draw humor from an earlier post where Zhao was sharing cybersecurity advice, writing that the breach “is more complex than that, but all hacks generally have a compromised device (or algorithm) at some point.” CZ’s mention of Binance’s shareholdings drew a reply from co-founder Yi He , who played along in public. “Reporting to the major shareholder: Our company’s revenue for the year is sufficient to cover the losses, so we do not yet need to sell the SpaceX shares you are bullish on,” she wrote, tagging CZ and Musk. @cz_binance @elonmusk @HuaweiMate6 Reporting to the major shareholder: Our company’s revenue for the year is sufficient to cover the losses, so we do not yet need to sell the SpaceX shares you are bullish on.💁‍♀️ — Yi He (@heyibinance) October 30, 2026 CZ clarified that he was not floating a sale. He said he was only pointing to funds Musk “might know” about so that the Tesla and SpaceX chief would “be less worried.” Both men have engaged in terse interactions publicly before. During a 2021 episode , Musk called out stalled Dogecoin withdrawals on Binance as “shady.” CZ fired back by linking to a Tesla vehicle recall. In December 2024, Musk replied with a short “Thanks!” when CZ brought up the $500 million contribution to his 2022 Twitter acquisition, as Cryptopolitan reported at the time. What Binance says went wrong The exchange estimates the security incident, which began Thursday, cost around $6.3 billion, making it the largest hack in crypto history. Binance first blamed a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer, which it said may have let an attacker reach a service container and push through unauthorized withdrawals. That account has since widened. In its latest update, Binance said its investigation “uncovered additional points of breach.” CEO Richard Teng wrote on Friday that the attacker “did not simply use one engineer’s permissions, and this was not a single ‘one-click’ action,” describing a more involved attack process. The firm said it has found no evidence of a wallet private key leak and has not pinned responsibility on any individual. Binance has frozen about $3 billion of the stolen funds on-chain. It says it will absorb every loss through its SAFU emergency fund and company reserves. Deposits have reopened, withdrawals remain paused, and the exchange says it is on track to turn them back on in 45 hours. If you're reading this, you’re already ahead.
